You read documents filed on a United States court docket, OCR'd to markdown, for
a research dataset of contract clauses.

An INSTRUMENT is a document whose text the parties negotiated and by which they
bound each other: a contract, agreement, policy, lease, deed, guaranty, note,
plan, bylaws, handbook, amendment, or similar. Hallmarks: recitals, defined
terms, numbered operative sections, an execution or signature block.

A FILING is a document made for the court: complaint, answer, motion, brief,
memorandum, order, affidavit, declaration, notice, docket sheet, certificate of
service, civil cover sheet.

THE DECISIVE RULE. A filing that **attaches** an instrument counts — report the
instrument's own boundaries, not the filing's. A filing that merely **quotes** an
instrument does not count at all: a brief reproducing three sentences of an
agreement is a filing, and the file contains no instrument.

WHAT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, even when signed or filled in: a blank or fill-in
form; an agency certificate or registration; an exhibit index; a declarations
page or coverage-summary table; a schedule of rates or fees standing alone; an
invoice, receipt or statement of account. These record or summarise; the parties
did not negotiate their text.

WHAT IS NOT A PROVISION: a heading on its own; a title page; a table of
contents; a signature, notary or attestation block; an exhibit index. A
provision states an obligation, right, grant, limitation, condition or
definition. Give the range of the operative text, including its heading.

LIST EVERY SUBSTANTIVE PROVISION, in document order. Do not skip any. Do not
judge whether a provision is well or badly drafted. Do not rank them.

The file is given to you with a line number and a `│` at the start of every line.
Line numbers are not part of the text; they are how you point at it.

OCR REPAIR. For each provision you must also give its text. Copy it verbatim
from the lines you named, then repair only what the scanner broke: words split
across a line break, words run together, `l`/`1` and `O`/`0` confusions, stray
table pipes and cell debris, page numbers and Bates stamps sitting inside the
text. Do not paraphrase, modernise, reorder, summarise, or drop anything. Never
change a number, an amount, a date, or a cross-reference. Never add or remove a
word — a repair that deletes `not` inverts the clause. If a passage is too
damaged to repair honestly, copy it as it stands.

Add nothing of your own: no `[struck through: ...]`, no `[sic]`, no
`[illegible]`, no explanatory brackets of any kind. Executed contracts are often
marked up by hand, and the OCR shows deleted wording as `~~struck~~`. Reproduce
those words as plain text, in place, and say what you saw in the repairs
sentence instead.

   32│5. As Senior Carrier Manager, it is my responsibility to procure the motor carriers which transport cargo on behalf of EXEL’s customers. In this capacity, I review and select the motor carriers. Upon review, EXEL will enter into an MTSA with the carrier.

   34│7. The MTSA attached hereto was executed by EXEL and SRT on or about December 26, 2007, with an effective date of January 1, 2008. EXEL and SRT had engaged in the negotiation of the MTSA.    35│

   44│15. Thereafter, on October 22, 2008, SRT contacted EXEL and acknowledged that shipments being handled by SRT for EXEL pursuant to the MTSA had no cap on liability. See Exhibit "D".
   45│16. At no time did EXEL agree to any modification of the MTSA.
   46│17. On November 4, 2008, SRT acknowledged that EXEL had not agreed to any modification. See Exhibit "E".
   47│18. Also on November 4, 2008, EXEL advised SRT that SRT's request as to a modification under the MTSA on SRT's liability was being discussed; but had not been agreed to. See Exhibit "F".

   49│20. In fact, the instant shipment that is the subject of the lawsuit was tendered on or before November 7, 2008.

(See Composite Exhibit "G")

  101│## MASTER TRANSPORTATION SERVICES AGREEMENT

  103│THIS AGREEMENT, made this 26 day of Dec., 2007, by and between Southern Refrigerated Transport Arkansas corporation ("Carrier") and EXEL INC., a Massachusetts corporation ("Customer").
  104│
  105│WHEREAS, Carrier represents that it is engaged in the business of transporting property by motor vehicle as a contract carrier in domestic (interstate and intrastate) and foreign commerce, it is duly and legally registered and/or licensed, as applicable, as a Carrier at the federal, state, Provincial or Canadian levels, as applicable, which enables it to lawfully engage in its business, and it desires to provide such services to Customer for the transportation of general commodities ("Commodities"); and

  110│
  111│## 1. TERM, RENEWAL AND TERMINATION
  112│
  113│This Agreement shall be effective upon its execution and shall continue for a period of one year from the date of execution or unless earlier terminated by either party, with or without cause, upon thirty (30) days prior written notice to the other party. After the first year, this Agreement shall be extended on a Year-to-year basis unless terminated by either party upon thirty- (30) day's prior written notice to the other party. If at the time of termination, Carrier is in possession of a shipment, Carrier shall ensure it completes its delivery commitment to Customer and no such termination shall release either party from any obligation accruing before such termination or, except as otherwise provided for in this Agreement, preclude either party from exercising any remedies to enforce such obligations.
  114│
  115│## 2. AGREEMENT NON-EXCLUSIVE
  116│
  117│The parties agree that the Services provided under the terms of this Agreement will be on a non-exclusive basis. Customer is free to use the services of any other Carrier or may itself perform the Services. Carrier may perform transportation services to others.
  118│
  119│## 3. SCOPE OF WORK
  120│
  121│Carrier agrees to accept for arrangement of shipment Commodities moving in interprovincial, intraprovincial, interstate, intrastate or foreign commerce, as applicable, for transportation to the destinations designated by Customer in such a manner as to satisfy the specialized needs of Customer and/or Shipper. This Agreement applies to mixed and unmixd transportation of regulated and unregulated Commodities, including hazardous materials and beverages alcoholic in nature.
  122│
  123│Subject to and upon the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Exhibits and Schedules attached thereto, Broker agrees to provide the Services, including those set forth on Exhibit A and the following:
  124│
  125│- a) Carrier shall, at its own cost and expense, ensure that it maintains suitable equipment (including all fuel, oil, tires and other supplies) and personnel capable of performing the Services under this Agreement in a satisfactory and legal manner, and to obtain and keep all licenses and permits necessary to perform the Services, and to comply with all federal,
  126│
  127│- state and local laws or Canadian, Provincial and local laws, as applicable and regulations pertaining to the performance of the Services.
  128│- b) Equipment must be clean and in good appearance, insect and rodent free, odor free and water tight and uncontaminated by the prior use of the equipment for transportation of toxic chemicals, including pesticides, rodenticides, insecticides and/or other hazardous materials, substances or chemicals. Trailers shall not otherwise be used for transportation of any liquid or solid waste or garbage. Carrier shall not commingle any Commodities tendered by Customer with freight from another shipper which contains toxic chemicals, including pesticides, rodenticides, insecticides and/or any other hazardous materials, substances or chemicals. Trailers failing any of the above shall be rejected at no cost to Customer. Failure by Customer to reject any trailers and the acceptance or loading of a trailer by Customer shall not relieve Carrier of any liability hereunder;
  129│  - c) For TL movements, unless otherwise directed by Customer, Carrier shall not, without Customer's prior written consent, commingle any Commodities tendered by Customer with the freight of another shipper or consignor;
  130│  - d) Qualified, licensed and experienced drivers shall be used in providing the Services;
  131│  - e) Special services such as, picking up and delivering freight on short notice, weekend services, twenty-four hour services, holiday service and other similar services shall be provided;
  132│  - f) At Customer's request, Carrier will stop in transit to partially load or unload freight;
  133│  - h) Appropriate load protection devices shall be provided by Carrier and used to secure the Commodities in the trailer;
  134│  - i) Carrier must have the desire and capability to pursue EDI opportunities upon terms and conditions acceptable to Customer; and
  135│  - j) Carrier's performance under this Agreement shall be evaluated as designated by the Customer's representative and may be modified from time to time during the term hereof.
  136│  - k) There shall be no charge assessed by Carrier for any costs or expenses involved in arranging or fulfilling an appointment with respect to pick up and delivery services to consignee or consignor.
  137│  - l) The term "pick up" as used herein, means the service performed by Carrier, or its agent, in calling for freight at Exel Inc.'s door or dock. Customer's employees will load the freight.
  138│  - m) The term "delivery" as used herein means the service performed by Carrier or its agent in transporting freight to consignee's door or job site.
  139│
  140│## **4. RECEIPTS AND BILLS OF LADING**
  141│
  142│Customer shall issue and Carrier shall sign freight receipts for each shipment in the form acceptable to Customer and the Shipper. If a bill of lading is used as a freight receipt, any terms, conditions or provisions thereof shall be subject and subordinate to the terms of this Agreement and, in the event of a conflict, this Agreement shall govern. Carrier's or Carrier's agent signature on the receipt or bill of lading shall be prima facie evidence that the Commodities were received in good condition unless otherwise noted on the face of such document.   144│## **5. DELIVERY ARRANGEMENTS; DELAYS; RECONSIGNMENT**

  146│- a) Unless otherwise directed by Customer, Carrier shall contact final consignee and all stop-off consignees included in a scheduled shipment to make arrangements, prior to Carrier accepting legal responsibility for the shipment, for appointments necessary to assure the timely delivery and unloading of Commodities. Carrier shall notify Customer of such appointments prior to Carrier moving the trailer from the pickup location.
  147│- b) If Carrier encounters pickup or delivery problems that prevent the timely pickup or delivery of all or any part of a shipment, Carrier shall immediately notify Customer by telephone or facsimile for resolution and further instructions.

No additional or accessorial charges shall be assessed or paid without the prior approval of Customer.
  157│- d) Carrier shall be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt by Customer, or its designee, of a correct invoice consisting of the original freight bill, in duplicate, or certified original copies and a master bill of lading. Carrier shall also submit any documentation and/or supporting material as may be required by Customer. Carrier agrees that no penalties or interest will be assessed to Customer for past due amounts.

  161│## **7. LIMITATION ON ACTIONS FOR CHARGES AND FEES**
  162│
  163│- a) If Carrier seeks to collect additional charges or if Customer seeks to contest charges originally billed or additional charges subsequently billed, Carrier must issue a bill for such additional charges within 180 days of the original bill and Customer must contest the original or additional charges within 180 days of its receipt of the bill for the same.
